Lessons.Title: Situations and Equations
ExplanationParagraphs: An unknown letter can represent a beginning quantity, the amount in each group, or a final result. The source's 2021 lesson compares THREE Mai bead stories that use nearly the same numbers but place the unknown differently.
Warm-up — Notice and Wonder: The Unknown. The original bar contains a total128 and three known parts each8, leaving a missing part128−3×8=104. Naming the missing part b does not change its value.
Activity 1 — Mai's Beads (20 minutes). Situation1: Mai starts with104 beads, buys two equal unknown packs and finishes with124. Equation104+2×n=124, so n=10 beads in EACH pack.

Situation2: Mai starts with an unknown, adds two packs of10 and finishes with124. Equation n+10+10=124, so n=104 starting beads. Situation3: Mai begins with104, buys two packs of10, and seeks the total. Equation104+2×10=n, so n=124 final beads.

Distinguish the corresponding original tape-bar source roles: (a) 104 with two unknown equal parts totaling124; (b) unknown initial plus two known10 parts totaling124; (c) 104 plus two known10 parts with unknown total. The archived descriptions reveal this mathematical structure without granting rights to the original figure pixels.

Activity2 — Represent, Solve, Explain (15 minutes). Kiran begins with104 mancala stones and removes3 for EACH of six pits: r=104−(6×3)=86 remain. Draw six equal 3-stone groups removed, label the jar's remaining count with an unknown letter, and verify 86+18=104.

Compare the pupil's word situation, diagram, equation and result. The teacher reviews the representations and explanations; numeric Edulytics checks are separate. Original publisher Mancala photograph and gated original How Many Beads? Cool-down not reproduced.

KeyConcepts.Title: Unknown per group
KeyConcepts.Definition: A variable naming one equal pack's contents.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Find the difference in total and divide by number of packs.

KeyConcepts.Title: Unknown initial value
KeyConcepts.Definition: A variable naming the starting quantity before known additions.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Subtract all known later additions from total.

KeyConcepts.Title: Unknown final value
KeyConcepts.Definition: A variable naming result after known changes.

KeyConcepts.Title: Represent groups removed
KeyConcepts.Definition: Subtraction of multiple equal groups uses multiplication for the total removed.

WorkedExamples.Title: One source story, unknown group size
WorkedExamples.Question: Mai has104, receives two equal unknown packs and ends124. What is in each?
WorkedExamples.Check: n is EACH pack, not the starting total.

WorkedExamples.Title: Initial unknown
WorkedExamples.Question: Mai ends124 after adding two packs of10. Initial amount?

WorkedExamples.Title: Mancala
WorkedExamples.Question: Kiran has104 stones and places3 in six pits. How many remain?
WorkedExamples.Check: The source asks for the jar remainder, not stones on board.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Use n=124 in all three Mai equations.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The unknown stands for distinct quantities across stories.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Determine whether n denotes each pack, starting amount or ending amount.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Subtract just3 stones from Mancala jar.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: There are6 pits with3 stones EACH.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Match diagram by color or layout instead of quantities.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Only the labeled relationships are mathematical invariants.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Check 104, two groups10 or unknown, and target124.

SummaryPoints: Teacher evaluates diagram/equation correspondence. Original images, PDF and gated source exit remain unverified.
